la:noun:anser.html:
anser, ĕris, usu. m.
Sanscr. hasas; Gr. χήν; Germ. Gans; Engl. Gander; Erse, goss = goose
(f., ; ; cf. Schneid. Gram. II. p. 7; Bentl. ad ; Neue, Formenl. I. p. 612 sq.),
a goose; sacred to Juno, and which preserved the Capitol in the Gallic war. Hence held in high honor by the Romans, ; ; —Anser Amyclaeus, the swan, into which Jupiter changed himself at Amyclœ, .

la:noun:ansa.html:
ansa, ae, f.
cf. χανδάνω, and pre-hendo, pre-hensum, and λαβή from λαβεῖν
,
that by which something is taken hold of, a handle, haft; of a vessel, pitcher, vase, and the like.
Lit., ; ; ; ; ; —Of other things, e. g. of an iron handle of a door: ansa ostii,.—Of the loop on the edge of a sandal, through which the shoetie was drawn, ; so .—Of the handle of the rudder, the tiller, .—Of the cheeks of a balance in which the lever moves, .— In architecture, the cramp-iron or brace which holds several stones together, ; .—
Trop., as also the Gr. λαβή, handle, occasion, opportunity (rare, and in the class. per. only in Cic.): illum quaerere ansam, infectum ut faciat?: reprehensionis ansa,: controversiarum,: ansas sermonis dare,: sibi tamquam ansas ad reprehendendum dare,: alicui lucrandi ansam offerre,.
